item.title: Climate-vulnerable Africa faces significant gaps in early warning systems, leaving millions at risk from extreme weather
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: Climate-related events affected at least 13 million people across Africa in 2025. Over the last decade alone, extreme weather has affected populations in Africa disproportionately. Tropical Cyclone Freddy (February 2023) caused widespread flooding and led to over 1,500 deaths, and in 2015–16 a drought in southern Africa led to widespread crop failure and food insecurity for 40 million people.

item.title: Historical records reveal the bitter truth about 17th-century Transylvania's climate
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: For roughly five centuries from about 1300, Europe experienced periods of unusually cold weather and extreme conditions collectively known as the Little Ice Age. Transylvania, a historical region in modern-day Romania, was also affected, but information about just how severe things were had been scattered in old town records, church logs, travelogs and administrative and monastic diaries.
